mechanism: SMOC EA estimates drift μ and volatility σ, then sets predictionHorizon = clamp(5,20, baseHorizon*(1+σ)). Expected return is simulated via GBM paths with Box–Muller shocks over that horizon; ATR scales dynamic SL/TP (buy SL = price−1.2·ATR·multi, TP = price+1.8·ATR·multi). Horizon length and stop distance both expand when realized vol rises.
data_needed: Close series for μ/σ and historical avg; ATR(14); successRate for decision threshold
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex generic _Symbol; backtests shown on D1, H1, H4, H6 (2020–2024)
why_new_for_mis: Couples a volatility-scaled MPC forecast window with ATR-geometry stops into one adaptive-horizon volatility sensor stack.

mechanism: From 25 FX pairs build ~2000 synthetic prices (bid1/ask2, bid1/bid2). Arbitrage flag when real bid − synthetic > 0.00008 (8 points). Separately, skip trading 23:30–05:00 because night liquidity is thinner and spreads widen—session clock as liquidity gate.
data_needed: Tick/M1 bid-ask for listed majors/crosses; MIN_SPREAD=0.00008; UTC clock
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AUDUSD,EURUSD,GBPUSD,USDJPY and 21 other FX pairs; live ticks + M1 backtest Jan–Aug 2024
why_new_for_mis: Treats synthetic-vs-quoted price gap plus overnight-hours veto as dual liquidity/mispricing sensors usable outside pure arb execution.

mechanism: OHLC closes → binary up/down directions. Patterns of length 3–25 are scored by outcome 6 bars ahead (True/False); keep patterns with frequency>20, rank by winrate, top-300 buy/sell. Live: current U/D string maps to historical buy/sell probability over lookback (default 1000) and forecast horizon (default 6).
data_needed: Close series; pattern_length 3–25 (or 3–10 in MQL5); lookback; forecast_horizon; min_occurrences
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H4 1990–2024; also D1/W1/MN1 proposed; multi-pair EA on 10 liquid FX
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a non-parametric sequence sensor: empirical P(up|direction-string) / P(down|…) as a soft directional prior from repeating binary path motifs.
quote: We take a data sample of pattern_length ... and look at what happens 6 bars after it.

mechanism: Features: vol_ma5/20, vol_ratio=real_volume/vol_ma20, volume_momentum(24), volume_volatility=std(pct_change(vol),24), price_volume_correlation(24). IsolationForest(contamination≈0.1) flags is_anomaly on scaled volume; KMeans(n=3) on [real_volume, vol_ratio, volatility] labels background/accumulation, run/movement, extreme clusters. Observed sequence: anomaly → cluster-3 → active volume → directional move (esp. post-open).
data_needed: real_volume + OHLC; IsolationForest + KMeans; optional session open clock
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: SBER (Sberbank) H1; ~365 days Russian equity market
why_new_for_mis: Combines unsupervised volume-anomaly bits with a 3-state volume-regime cluster—liquidity-flow sensing beyond raw OBV/CMF.
quote: Three clusters were chosen because I would conditionally divide all volumes into "background or accumulation" volumes, "run and movement" volumes, and "extreme movement" volumes.

mechanism: 2-layer LSTM(hidden=64, dropout=0.2) + linear head consumes [vol_ratio, vol_ma5, volatility, volume_cluster, is_anomaly, price_momentum, volume_momentum, volume_volatility, price_volume_correlation] to predict next-period return. Signal if |pred|>0.1%; stops use predicted_volatility: max(|pred|*0.7, pred_vol*1.5). Author notes consecutive signal runs precede strong moves and fixed thresholds fail when average vol soars.
data_needed: Volume/price feature window (lookback 24); LSTM weights; predicted_return & predicted_volatility
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: SBER H1; Russian stocks; hour filter 10–12 optional
why_new_for_mis: End-to-end neural volume→return sensor with explicit high-vol threshold-break failure mode—useful MIS sequence head on liquidity features.
quote: It is precisely when most traders prefer to stay out of the market that the neural network finds the clearest patterns in the volume flow.

mechanism: Each day scan bars from midnight to 6AM; max(open,close) and min(open,close) over that window define upper/lower range. After scanBarTime, if prior-bar close > max (or < min) within validBreakTime_start…end (default through 11AM / hoursValidity), flag breakout and trade (SL at opposite bound, TP = r2r×range). One breakout flag per day; optional invert direction.
data_needed: Intraday bars from D1 midnight; sixAM + hoursValidity; open/close of session bars
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex generic; designed for H1 or H4; Asian→London/NY session logic
why_new_for_mis: Session-anchored range membership then timed breakout is a clean regime-change event sensor (range → directional break) for MIS.
quote: A breakout occurs when the price moves above an established resistance level or below a support level.

mechanism: Implements GD, momentum GD, SGD, and Levenberg–Marquardt for MLP regression on synthetic y=1+sin(π/4·t)+N(0,σ²). Compares speed vs sklearn SGD/Adam/L-BFGS. Mentions online bar-by-bar retrain as motivation but builds no market-state sensor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic 81-point and 1000×2-feature datasets; no live market instrument
why_new_for_mis: Full read: neural-net optimizer tutorial on synthetic data; no regime/vol/liquidity sensing construction.
quote: All subsequent examples use synthetic data for ease of presentation.

mechanism: Seven features normalized to [−1,1]: bar range/close, 12-bar vol, 24-bar momentum, sin/cos(2π·hour/24), close/SMA deviation, latest return. Encoded as RY angles on 3 qubits with CNOT entanglement (Python/Qiskit) or classical state-probability simulation (MQL5, SHOTS≈2000). Weighted vote of 8 basis states yields signed prediction; |pred|<InpMinConfidence (0.15) → neutral. Stronger in high-vol regimes per author.
data_needed: OHLC, returns, SMA, hour-of-day; NUM_QUBITS=3; SHOTS; min_confidence
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD (yfinance + MT5); H1 example setups; multi-session EA
why_new_for_mis: Maps a compact multi-feature vector into an 8-state probability mass with confidence gating—a soft multi-regime neural/sequence-style sensor.
quote: Market data is encoded into quantum states via RY (rotation) gates, representing market characteristics as quantum superpositions.

mechanism: Meta-features = rolling skewness of close (periods_meta, default 10). KMeans(n_clusters≈5–10) assigns market modes on train window only. For each cluster: (1) CatBoost direction model on MA features of that cluster’s labeled mean-reversion examples; (2) meta CatBoost on skew features predicts binary “in this cluster?” Gate trades only when meta_sig>0.5 for the chosen mode.
data_needed: Close H1; rolling skew; KMeans labels; CatBoost/ONNX dual models
why_new_for_mis: Uses distribution skew clustering as an explicit market-mode sensor that gates a separate directional model—clean two-layer regime stack for MIS.
quote: Skew clustering allows one to identify groups of data with similar distribution characteristics, which helps identify these modes.

mechanism: Savitzky–Golay (or spline/SMA) smooths close; lvl=close−smoothed. Quantile bands (e.g. 0.45/0.55 or rolling quantiles) define reversion zones: lvl>q_high → sell label, lvl<q_low → buy. Variants: multi-period filters, bidirectional asymmetric windows, volatility-group quantiles (20 vol buckets), and profit-restricted labels requiring future markup success.
data_needed: Close series; rolling window; quantiles; optional markup/min_l/max_l; volatility_window
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURGBP H1 (flat pair focus); also general FX
why_new_for_mis: Turns non-causal filter residual vs adaptive quantile bands into a principled mean-reversion excursion/change sensor for labeling and live gating.
quote: When the upper and lower bands cross, a sell or buy signal is formed. If the price crosses the upper line, it is a sell signal.

mechanism: MF multiplier=[(C−L)−(H−C)]/(H−L); MFV=MF·volume; n-period CMF=ΣMFV/ΣVol ∈[−1,1]. Sensors: (1) zero-line cross (prev<0 & curr>0 buy / opposite sell); (2) OB/OS at ±0.20; (3) CMF>0 with price crossing above MA (and mirror) as trend-validated flow. Best backtest: CMF+MA validation on EURUSD M15.
data_needed: H/L/C + tick or real volume; CMF period 20; OB/OS ±0.20; optional MA period
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M15, 2023 full year; SL 300 / TP 900 points
why_new_for_mis: Classic Chaikin money-flow as bounded accumulation/distribution oscillator with zero and ±0.20 liquidity-regime thresholds for MIS.
quote: A positive Chaikin Money Flow result is when the price action consistently closes above the bar's midpoint on rising volume.

mechanism: From a backtest deal list compute per-trade % balance change. Shuffle order many times (e.g. 1000), recompute equity paths (final equity invariant by commutativity), collect max-drawdown distribution; use ~95th percentile as live risk tolerance to set fractional Kelly risk %. Multi-EA: Kelly fractions f=Σ⁻¹μ from return covariance across strategies.
data_needed: Backtest profit/balance series; shuffle count; target DD tolerance (e.g. 30%); multi-EA return panels
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Example XAU and multi-EA CSV panels (DBG-XAU/SP/EU); MQL5 risk% lot sizing
why_new_for_mis: Path-order Monte Carlo maxDD percentile is a strategy-risk sensor that converts one equity curve into a drawdown-regime prior for sizing—orthogonal to price-path regime.
quote: We choose the 95% percentile because it's a general result scholars see as close to live trading performance.

mechanism: Five randomness/trend criteria on N prices: Abbe (sample var vs Allan-like successive-diff var—presence only); sign-of-first-differences (with optional time weights) as overbought/oversold via empirical distribution thirds; Kendall pairwise sign sums (direction+strength); Wald–Wolfowitz rank autocorrelation; Foster–Stewart top/bottom record counts T (direction) and D (presence), optionally T·D for strongest trends. Extreme criterion → fade (mean-revert after strong trend); Abbe+avg speed as trend filter.
data_needed: Close (or mid) window of length iPeriod; empirical quantile levels (e.g. 33% tails); optional pre-smoother tSMA/tEMA
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic FX price series; EA variants over selectable criteria/periods
why_new_for_mis: Provides a battery of nonparametric trend-presence and trend-direction sensors that do not assume Gaussian returns—strong MIS regime alternatives to ADX.
quote: The criterion allows us to check how random the price series is. If the criterion shows us that the series is not random, then we can say that it is a trend.

mechanism: Components: volatility=rolling std of returns(20); momentum=pct_change(5); volume_trend=tick_volume/SMA(volume,20); session_coef={Asian 0.7, European 1.0, American 0.9}. trend_force=vol·volume_trend·|momentum|·session_coef, normalized ~[3,9]. Levels: <3 quiet, 3–6 emerging, >6 full strength. Direction = sign(momentum)×force. Reversal pattern: force>6 and rolling std of direction_strength diffs >1.5, confirmed if volume_trend > 1.5× its MA.
data_needed: OHLC + tick_volume; MA 20; momentum 5; hour-of-day; thresholds 3/6
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic; author notes H1/H4 clearest; Python + MQL5 TrendForceIndicator
why_new_for_mis: Multiplies vol × relative volume × |momentum| with session weights into a single trend-force regime sensor with explicit pre-reversal oscillation signature.
